title: Why · How · What
caption: Hand AI a big job and it comes back looking right: why you stay in the loop, how, and a workflow to try.

why.title: The AI hands back a result that looks right and is not.
why.caption: <marker>Lawyers once filed a brief citing six cases ChatGPT had invented.</marker> It looked right, and nobody checked.

how.title: Split the job into stages and check each one.
how.caption: <marker>Break the task into steps, write the requirements down, let the AI ask before it starts, and review every step, not only the end.</marker>

what.title: A workflow where AI chats do the jobs and you steer.
what.caption: <marker>Each stage copies a prompt for a fresh chat, and you check its result before the next stage.</marker> Try the project plan above.

why.header: Unchecked output has cost real money
why.description: In a New York federal case, lawyers filed a brief citing six cases ChatGPT had invented and were fined; the court held that rules give attorneys a gatekeeping role for the accuracy of their filings [1]. In one study, programmers with an AI assistant wrote less secure code and were more sure it was secure, a result a larger study disputes [2] (research AIE-0005, AIE-0010).

castel-mata-v-avianca.title: Judge P. Kevin Castel, Mata v. Avianca, Inc., Opinion and Order, No. 22-cv-1461 (S.D.N.Y. June 22, 2023)

perry-insecure-code.title: Perry et al., Do Users Write More Insecure Code with AI Assistants?

how.header: Small steps, stated needs, step checks
how.description: Models often solve each sub-problem yet fail to compose them, and decomposing helps [1]. A stated requirement is met more steadily than a guessed one [2]. Clarifying questions raise accuracy on underspecified tasks [3]. Step-level checks catch flaws that a check of the final answer passes [4] (research AIE-0007, AIE-0008, AIE-0009, AIE-0010).

zhou-least-to-most.title: Zhou et al., Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in Large Language Models

yang-what-prompts-dont-say.title: Yang et al., What Prompts Don't Say: Understanding and Managing Underspecification in LLM Prompts

vijayvargiya-ambig-swe.title: Vijayvargiya et al., Ambig-SWE: Interactive Agents to Overcome Underspecificity in Software Engineering

lightman-verify-step-by-step.title: Lightman et al., Let's Verify Step by Step

what.header: Fresh chat per stage, checked in between
what.description: Accuracy falls as a chat grows, and a model that took a wrong turn leans on its earlier answers, so a fresh, focused context per job helps [1]; the answer to a step can be right while the reasoning is wrong, so an outside reader checks each artifact [2] (research AIE-0011, AIE-0010).
